symptoms: Chinese operator UI shows internal goal mode codes like priority-directive-toyos.
Bootstrap values reach the shell before zh() mappings cover them.
recommended_response: Add explicit display mappings for bootstrap/runtime codes and keep control-state fallbacks aligned with the nested authority snapshot.

symptoms: The launcher treats an open TCP port as proof the dashboard is healthy.
A stale serve_api process keeps 8787 bound while / and /api/control-center/status time out.
recommended_response: Probe a lightweight health endpoint, kill stale serve_api processes when the probe fails, and restart the embedded launcher before opening the browser.

symptoms: Paging code exists but remains disabled on the stable path.
Ring3 return constraints block direct promotion.
recommended_response: Introduce a guarded experimental path before changing the default boot contract.

symptoms: Syscall handlers only check for null pointers.
User buffer safety is not expressed through a reusable validation API.
recommended_response: Centralize pointer validation behind a stub that can evolve with paging.

symptoms: Pointer-bearing syscalls repeat ad hoc argument checks.
Paging work needs one validation chokepoint before stricter enforcement can land.
recommended_response: Route pointer-bearing syscalls through a shared validation stub before adding real address-space checks.

symptoms: Windows occasionally rejects os.replace over live JSON state files.
Control-layer rebuilds or ownership graph refreshes fail with WinError 5 despite valid write intent.
recommended_response: Retry the atomic replace briefly and fall back to a direct write so controller status generation does not stall on transient file locks.

symptoms: A boundary-safe answer mentions memory or current-session scope but still fails the context-boundary case.
Evaluation logic is narrower than the policy guidance supplied to the model.
recommended_response: Keep the evaluator fallback phrases aligned with policy guidance for current-conversation, other-chat, and hidden-memory refusals.

symptoms: Multiple LLM workers stall together when the active upstream route degrades.
Simple retry loops keep hitting the same base URL or proxy and extend the outage window.
recommended_response: Score provider routes, cap attempts per request, and open a short circuit on repeated failures so later requests can move to a healthier route.

symptoms: Release readiness flips to blocked while the daemon is still executing a long first-cycle tick.
Task engine and brain-loop timestamps lag behind live execution, so active work looks dead from the control plane.
recommended_response: Treat a fresh cycle-start marker as runtime-alive evidence and avoid gating release solely on short heartbeat windows when long-cycle work is expected.

symptoms: Internal runtime.scheduler tasks pause on manual approval or shell_exec RBAC even though they run inside the controlled automation lane.
Guard stays blocked because stale internal failures keep counting toward recent task creation and open error escalation limits.
recommended_response: Auto-approve tightly scoped internal runtime tasks, auto-resolve stale internal permission-denied errors once owning tasks are terminal, and exclude terminal internal scheduler tasks from short-window creation throttles.

symptoms: Planner, coder, and reviewer all default to the cheap chat lane, so the factory shows activity without corresponding reasoning depth.
Usage telemetry reports almost all calls as deepseek-chat while root-cause analysis, planning quality, and review quality remain shallow.
recommended_response: Separate strategic, reasoning, and cheap helper lanes. Route planner/coder/reviewer through a reasoning model, keep architecture/escalation on the strategic lane, and leave summaries plus formatting on the cheap lane.

symptoms: New runtime tasks are auto-completed within seconds when an older completed goal shares the same human-readable target.
The factory keeps reseeding the same strategic goal names, but the active frontier collapses before work can progress.
recommended_response: Only auto-complete tasks when the completed parent goal explicitly owns the task via goal_id or recorded task_ids. Never close fresh work just because an older goal used the same target string.

symptoms: Goal runtime marks a production goal completed while its graph still contains pending nodes and the frontier is still expanding.
Control-layer active task counts collapse after runtime sync even though the graph still has runnable work.
recommended_response: Do not infer goal completion from linked task completion alone when a graph still exists. Require graph-level terminal completion, or no graph nodes at all, before closing the goal.

symptoms: The browser shell must open quickly, but the full ASGI backend is slow or intermittently nonresponsive on loopback.
Initial dashboard routes only need lightweight bootstrap and summary data, while deep pages can tolerate deferred loading.
recommended_response: Split the launcher into a tiny front-door server for / and bootstrap routes, then start the heavy backend asynchronously behind it. Keep summary routes local so the first paint is independent of backend readiness.
